text:
B: Hello. Can you hear me okay?
A: Er, yeah. Yeah, I can hear you fine.
B: Good. I am Tomasz. I think we start, yes? Three minutes.
A: Aye. Gareth. Erm, I'm in Wrexham.
B: Wrexham, okay. I am in Warrington, so not so far. We used to go to North Wales for caravan holidays, near Rhyl, a few times.
A: Oh right. Yeah, we go to Abersoch most summers, sort of the same thing really. Caravan park.
B: It is nice there. Very windy, I remember. So what do you do, Gareth?
A: Erm, admin, basically. Transport office at a building supplies place on the industrial estate. I book the deliveries in, do the dispatch spreadsheet, chase the drivers for their paperwork. That sort of thing, you know.
B: Ah, so you are the one who knows where every lorry is.
A: Supposed to be. Not always, like.
B: I did similar, actually. Eleven years shift supervisor at a warehouse near Birchwood. Delivery notes, rotas. When one lorry does not come, everybody shouts at you.
A: Yeah. Yeah, that's it. I just sort of don't panic, you know. They turn up eventually.
B: That is the right way, I think. Panic does not bring the lorry faster.
A: No. So you're not there now, then?
B: No. Now I am student, if you can believe it. Second year, civil engineering at Salford. I am forty-four and everybody on my course is maybe nineteen, twenty. So I am like the uncle in the library. But it is good. I wanted to do it for a long time, and I treat it like a job, you know, nine until four, then home.
A: Fair play. That's, erm... that's a big thing to do.
B: It is. Some days I think, what am I doing. But okay.
A: I did a year of college, IT. Never finished it. Sort of wonder sometimes, but I dunno, really.
B: Maybe is not too late. Look at me.
A: Maybe. Erm. Is the M62 bad, getting to Salford?
B: Terrible. Every morning. You have traffic too?
A: Half four on the industrial estate, it's a nightmare. Everyone tries to get out the same road.
B: Same everywhere. I saw in your photo, a dog bed. You have a dog?
A: Yeah, Dot. Staffy. She chewed through the telly remote cable last week, so, er, that was fun.
B: Oh no. Good dog otherwise?
A: Yeah, she's soft as anything. I walk her round the block most nights. She needs it, more than me, like.
B: I walk also, every evening on the Sankey Valley trail. No dog. My son wants one, but my brother's wife says no, so no.
A: Fair enough. Her house, her rules, I suppose.
B: Exactly. And the scarf, Wrexham, you go to the matches?
A: Few times a season, with my dad. Watch the rest on the telly. You into football?
B: A bit. Legia Warszawa, from home. And here I like Warrington Wolves, the rugby. A friend from work took me once and...
